chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ismāʿīl, from Yūnus, from some of his men, from Abū ʿAbdillāh and Abū Jaʿfar, peace be upon them, who said:
“The shroud obligatory for men is three garments, while the turban and the binding cloth are sunnah (recommended). As for women, their obligatory shroud is five garments.”

key_terms.اَلْخِرْقَةُ: the binding cloth mentioned as recommended in the shrouding
key_terms.اَلْعِمَامَةُ: the turban cloth added to the male shroud as a recommended practice
key_terms.اَلْكَفَنُ: the burial shroud used for the deceased
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَثْوَابٍ: three garments required for a male shroud
key_terms.خَمْسَةُ أَثْوَابٍ: five garments required for a female shroud
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended practice, not legally obligatory

ai.seo_question: How many shroud garments are obligatory for men and women in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling for the kafan of the deceased. It distinguishes between the obligatory number of shroud garments for men and women, while also noting that the turban and binding cloth for men are sunnah (recommended), not obligatory.
